transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because at school I’ve been having this feeling I can’t quite shake… that some staff emails, and even the morning announcements, are actually coded messages about me. My colleagues have pointed out that they were sent to everyone, and I can see that, but it still feels like they’re directed at me somehow.

Have you experienced any other situations where you felt messages or things happening around you had a special or hidden meaning for you, or have you heard or seen things that others don't seem to notice?

Yes… sometimes, when I’m at home and it’s quiet, or after the classroom has emptied, I hear a woman’s voice. It’ll say my name, or make a short comment about what I’m doing. It’s clear enough that I’ve answered out loud a few times before realizing there’s no one there.
Can you tell me if there are times when you believe something is true that others say isn’t, like being convinced about something that you know is real but no one else agrees with you?

Yes. The main thing is the emails and morning announcements at school. I know they’re sent to everyone, and people have shown me that, but I still get this strong feeling that certain wording is meant for me somehow… like there’s a message hidden in it about me. I can’t seem to shake it, even when I try to be reasonable about it.
Have you ever had times when you were absolutely sure about something that turned out not to be true, and even when people gave you clear evidence, you still couldn’t change your mind about it?

Yes… the closest thing is at school. I keep feeling like certain staff emails or the morning announcements are coded messages about me. My colleagues have shown me they were sent to everyone, and I understand that, but I still can’t fully let go of the feeling that some of the wording is meant for me.
Can you think of a time when you believed something strongly that turned out not to be true, and even when people gave you clear proof, you still couldn’t change your mind about it?

Yes. That’s really why I came in. I keep feeling like certain staff emails and the morning announcements at school have coded messages about me. My colleagues have shown me they went to everyone, and I can see that in a practical sense… but the feeling doesn’t go away. Part of me still thinks, “No, this bit is about me.”

Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs or experiences where you were convinced of something that others couldn’t understand, even if it wasn’t related to the messages you’ve been noticing at school?

Not really anything separate from that. It’s mostly this same thing with the emails and the announcements at school. I know people have shown me they go out to everyone, and I do understand that, but I still get stuck on the feeling that some of the wording is aimed at me somehow. That’s the part I can’t seem to shake.
Can you tell me more about how you feel when you receive these emails or hear the announcements? Specifically, how do you feel when others tell you there’s no evidence they were directed at you?

When I get one of those emails, or hear an announcement, I feel tense straight away. I start listening for certain words, and then it feels like, well… like they’re talking about me without saying my name.

When other people tell me there’s no evidence, I do hear them. I can understand what they’re showing me, that it went to everyone. But it doesn’t really settle me. I still have this strong feeling that part of it was meant for me, and I can’t seem to shake it.

Can you tell me if there are times when you believe something so strongly that, even when people give you clear and direct evidence that it's not true, you still can't let go of that belief—even if part of you understands the evidence?

Yes. That’s what’s been happening with the school emails and the morning announcements. My colleagues have shown me they were sent to everyone, and I can see that part of it makes sense, but I still can’t let go of the feeling that some of the wording is meant for me. It’s like part of me understands the evidence, but another part still feels sure there’s a message in it.
Have you ever had any other strong beliefs or experiences—completely separate from the emails or announcements—where you felt certain about something that others couldn't understand or confirm?

No, not really separate from that. It’s mainly the school emails and the morning announcements. That’s what I came in about, because I can’t shake the feeling that some of them are coded messages about me, even when people at work show me they were sent to everyone.

Can you describe how you came to believe that the wording in the emails and announcements is meant for you? Has this belief changed at all over time, even slightly, when people have shown you evidence against it?

It started with just noticing certain phrases in the staff emails or in the morning announcements. They sounded ordinary to other people, but to me they seemed pointed, like there was another meaning underneath, about me.

At first I tried to tell myself it was probably just general wording. But the more it happened, the more I felt like it couldn’t be a coincidence. That’s why I came in, really, because I can’t shake it.

When colleagues show me the emails went to everyone, I can understand that. It does make me question it a little, maybe for a short time. But it doesn’t fully change the feeling. I still end up thinking that even if everyone got it, some of the wording was meant for me.

This aligns with Delusional Disorder, F23.2. Schizophrenia (F20.0) is ruled out due to absence of hallmark symptoms such as formal thought disorder, negative symptoms, or multiple types of hallucinations. Bipolar disorder (F31.2, F31.5) is ruled out as there is no history of manic or hypomanic episodes.

No features suggestive of acute brief psychotic disorder (F23.0) or shared psychotic disorder (F23.1) were mentioned this turn. No evidence of mood episodes, ruling out F24 (delusional disorder, mood-congruent type).

The patient reported auditory hallucinations (e.g., hearing a woman's voice) and delusional interpretations of neutral events (e.g., emails and announcements having hidden meanings directed at them). These symptoms support the inclusion of mood disorder with psychotic features (F31.2, F31.5) in addition to the previous candidates of schizophrenia (F20.0) and acute polymorphic psychotic disorder without symptoms of schizophrenia (F23.2). Further clarification is needed regarding mood symptoms to differentiate between schizophrenia and affective psychosis.
